claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The local chemical fluctuations in hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 are observable through detailed microstructural mapping.
A reduced-order multiscale model can integrate graph-based microstructural descriptors with targeted ab initio and experimental training data.
Controlled thermomechanical treatments can ensure a consistent hierarchical microstructure across tested HfNbTiVAl10 samples.
Graph-based representations can capture the relevant local chemical and microstructural fluctuations.
Local heterogeneities influence elastic behavior.
Local heterogeneities influence plastic behavior.
Local heterogeneities influence fracture behavior.
Embedding physically meaningful descriptors in a surrogate ML architecture reduces reliance on high-throughput quantum calculations.
The proposed framework will predict Young’s modulus of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately and efficiently than CALPHAD and full ab initio methods.
The proposed framework will predict yield strength of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately and efficiently than CALPHAD and full ab initio methods.
The proposed framework will predict toughness of hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately and efficiently than CALPHAD and full ab initio methods.
The framework is expected to improve yield-strength predictive accuracy by 20–30%.
The framework is expected to improve toughness predictive accuracy by 20–30%.
The framework is expected to reduce computational resource demands by at least 50% relative to ab initio or CALPHAD-based methods.
Full-scale ab initio calculations have high computational overhead and are difficult to deploy for high-throughput alloy prediction.
CALPHAD can require significant computational resources and can be limited by the availability of reliable databases for high-entropy alloys.
Existing generic machine-learning models have limited ability to model local chemical fluctuations.
The model may lose reliability when microstructural maps do not represent the relevant local fluctuations.
Sparse ab initio training data may make the model unreliable for rare crack-initiation phenomena.
